newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan growth eases to five percent in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan growth eases to five percent in 96/97.

text.p: Uganda on Thursday posted overall gross domestic product (GDP) growth at 5.0 percent in 1996/97 compared to 8.2 percent in 1995/96 and forecast modest growth of around 7.0 percent in 1997/98 (July/June).

Finance Minister Jehoash Mayanja-Nkangi told parliament deterioration in security in northern and southwestern Uganda on account of civil wars, drought in some areas, coffee and cassava diseases and unusually heavy rains that destroyed crops in western Uganda combined to cause "great economic sorrow".

Nkangi was presenting his state 1997/98 budget. He posted underlying inflation that excludes food prices at 1.9 percent in 1996/97 but said overall inflation was up at 11.8 percent from a single digit in 1995/96. He forecast average inflation at a lower 7.5 percent in 1997/98.

He said that the government wanted to contain inflation at around 5.0 percent in the future. He gave as a measure of the tight food supply situation an overall 30 percent rise in the price of food items but said a decline was expected soon.

Nkangi said Uganda's total external debt stood at $3.59 billion at end-December 1996 but added that under a World Bank and International Monetary Fund programme of debt relief for heavily indebted poor countries, Uganda would gain a reduction of more than $700 million as early as April 1998.

In 1996/97, Nkangi said he now expected revenues of 773 billion shillings, 43 billion lower than his budget forecast. That compared with expenditures of 1.203 billion, compared to earlier budgetary provisions of 1.172 billion shillings.

Nkangi said he was budgeting for revenues of 840 billion shillings in 1997/98 (excluding taxes on government and donor- funded procurements). Of that a total of 829 billion would come from taxes administered by the Uganda Revenue Authority and the balance from appropriations in aid.
He put overall government expenditure forecasts at 922 billion shillings.
